title: The Smile of Old Chapel Road
premise: August Villalobos takes a teaching post at Hollow Creek School, where a class vanished in 1911 and the founders' portraits smile a little too widely. When the mirrors begin lagging reality by one second, August and three students — the outcasts who've become their found family — discover the missing class was fed to the well beneath Old Chapel Road, and the well is refilling. To save this year's disappearing students, they must complete the founders' interrupted binding ritual from inside the reflection itself. August chooses to stay behind as the ritual's anchor so the children can cross back, trading their name for the town's silence — until the students, refusing to abandon family, pull them through at the last second, leaving the well sealed and the mirrors honest.
about_author: Ulyana Marchetti is a former rural schoolteacher who writes horror about institutions that remember more than the people inside them. She lives near an old chapel road of her own and has never once counted its doors.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: August's POV. Arriving at Hollow Creek, August notices the roster lists students who no one remembers, doors that must be counted nightly, and a janitor who warns them never to teach past dusk. Three lonely students — Devi, Marcus, and quiet Odile — gravitate to August's classroom. The emotional beat is wary belonging: August, rootless themselves, begins to care, even as the first mirror flickers half a heartbeat slow.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Devi's POV interleaved with August's. The lag widens: reflections move independently, showing the 1911 classroom mid-lesson. Researching in the chapel archive, the four learn the founders bound something under the well using the vanished class as anchors — and the binding is failing as enrollment drops. A student goes missing during a fire drill that no one else recalls happening. The beat is dread sharpening into resolve: they decide to finish what the founders started.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Following the reflections' instructions, they descend through the school's sealed cellar into the dry well, where the 1911 class still stands mid-ritual, smiling the founders' smile. The water rises as they chant the broken liturgy; Marcus is nearly taken, saved when August steps into the anchor's place. The climax: the ritual demands a keeper, and August offers themselves, the mirrors going perfectly still.

chapters.title: Counted Doors
chapters.summary: Shared POV, rotating line by line among the three students. Inside the reflection, August holds the door open while the children — living and from 1911 — walk out; Devi, Marcus, and Odile refuse the rule that keepers stay, hauling August back through as the well seals with a sound like a held breath released. Epilogue: spring term, full attendance, mirrors exactly on time. The beat is earned homecoming: justice done outside any law, inheritance refused, family chosen and kept.
